remaining_scientific_dependencies: The electron-redistribution candidate fails when coupled to the fixed optical mean: training improves but the held ninth-group statistic and raw residual RMS worsen. It is not an adequate telescope/detector response or an identified universal charge coefficient.

The shared-scene mean remains inadequate and the joint continuation remains nonstationary with active positivity bounds. Local unconstrained curvature is neither fully calibrated precision nor coverage validation.

Native per-read linearity Jacobians/Jensen corrections, SIRS spatial and reference covariance, gain uncertainty, dark/reference covariance, signal-dependent selection and padded-context uncertainty remain outside the working read covariance.

The deterministic electron-transport mean does not specify a stochastic transport law. Transfer-induced interpixel/time noise covariance is absent from the frozen ideal Poisson/CDS working covariance; mean conservation alone does not supply that statistical relation.

Actual quasar read histories and a jointly adequate optical/extended-light/history operator are still required before transferring this field coefficient. No such histories or transfer are fabricated.
All F115W photons and internal holdout groups/exposures here are already consumed development data. Re-reduction does not create genuinely unused observations.

This classical optical measurement calculation does not solve the microscopic U,V preparation or supply an inclusive statistical state kernel. Separate physical admission and downstream statistics are unchanged.
